name: Weakened signal: S1 geometry with strong guided deceleration
note: HYPOTHETICAL TEST POINT - not an official AYAP-1 target
epoch_definition: epoch_utc is the impact (emission) time at the lunar surface; photons reach each station 1.2-1.4 s later (per-site reception times below)
rationale: Kinetic energy reduced ~4.9x relative to ballistic; steeper impact; larger timing uncertainty

reachability.note: the impact is possible at this epoch only if the orbit plane is within the cross-track tolerance of the required node AND the orbital phase puts the spacecraft over the point; given the plane, passes over the latitude recur every orbital period.

terrain.dem: none: no LOLA product could be obtained in the analysis environment, so no site-specific terrain test is made
terrain.note: illustrative sensitivity: Earth above the horizon of 150 synthetic Gaussian-relief patches per declared relief level at the geocentric emission angle; not a validated lunar prior and not a bound (real terrain can raise or lower the horizon)

flash_magnitude_note: unocculted source-equivalent magnitudes at the geocentric distance (not apparent magnitudes if the point is occulted or behind the limb)

lab_trend.note: Swift et al. (2011) laboratory fit eta = 1.5e-3 exp(-(9.3/v)^2) for Pyrex into regolith simulant at 2.4-5.75 km/s, extrapolated below its tested range; T0 3000 K, tau 0.5 s. Under this case the flash is far below every detection limit.

plume.regime: sunlight only far above the surface
plume.instrument: 1-m telescope, V band, 1-s exposures, throughput 0.5, seeing 1.5 arcsec; background-subtraction systematic 1e-3 and 1e-2 of the background

plume.note: Housen & Holsapple (2011) point-source scaling with its domain [n1 a, n2 R]; two oblique-impact rules bracket a grazing impact by a hollow spacecraft, for which no validated rule exists; impactor bulk density is a calibration choice (the LCROSS like-for-like check favours ~400 kg/m3), not a validation.

crater.note: envelope over the Holsapple (LPI) and Housen & Holsapple (2011) parameter sets, bulk densities 150/400/1000 kg/m3 and the two oblique-impact rules; neither rule is validated for a hollow spacecraft at grazing incidence

latency.telemetry_note: direct-to-Earth S/X-band: the last frames before loss of signal arrive ~1.3 s after emission, plus ground processing (assumed 5-60 s); no relay, so no post-impact telemetry
latency.broadcast_note: broadcast (encoding/streaming) latency is separate from the light time: assumed 10-60 s

population.definition: sum of GeoNames-reported settlement populations whose coordinates meet the criteria; not a census, lower bound or audience estimate

lro.p_note: assumed probability that LRO is still operating in 2028 (scenario input, not measured; not a probability of imaging the crater)
lro.latency_summary: well-located near-side or mid-latitude impacts: first documented image after 0.6-11 days; far-side, high-latitude or poorly located impacts: about 2-4 months; public release 12-193 days after the event
lro.latency_note: heuristic from a small, selected precedent sample (impacts only; first documented image, release counted from the event); not a calibrated forecast for this site
lro.season_note: approximate orbit-plane illumination season (+-3 weeks model spread); does not guarantee a sunlit pass over this point

A_turkiye_priority.description: Turkish facilities only (TUG T100+QHY, RTT150 fast, DAG, university/amateur stations); TUG T100 streamed live

B_global_science.description: all professional stations worldwide with fast or NIR cameras plus NELIOTA and MIDAS; no amateur stations; TUG T100 and NELIOTA streamed

C_public_participation.description: Turkish stations, NELIOTA, MIDAS and amateur-class stations at every site (public venues), with streaming from TUG, NELIOTA and three amateur venues

public.phone_note: steady-source limits in the unfiltered (broad) CMOS band, not V magnitudes; flash detection also depends on the frame rate and processing
